clue.text: Mail chief of police initially over small criminal matters

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word police

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A police chief meddles in petty crimes, apparently connected with the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges S plus MATTERS into STMASTER, after P (first of police) and O (cricket's over).
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a post office is its master, the official in charge of the mail.

clue.text: Criticise adopting student's scheme

indicators.note: adopting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
L, the learner plate, stands for a student; the 's is 'has', a link

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a student's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts L inside PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme and a plan are synonyms for an arranged intention or design.

clue.text: Dot finally finishes drink

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word finishes

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone named Dot finally polishes off a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to mark a surface with many small dots, an art technique.

clue.text: Various men upset with local issue

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Assorted men are troubled by a matter of local concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MEN, LOCAL and ISSUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a mixed assortment of differing kinds, as in miscellaneous items.

clue.text: Observe reportedly natural energy in a boat?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: to observe is to see
born, as in a born leader, means natural
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Watch, so they say, natural energy at work in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns SEE into its sound-alike SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried on the sea by ship is borne by water, a playful paraphrase of being on board.

clue.text: Conservative quitting stops moderates

indicators.note: quitting means leaving, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: A Tory resigns and stops the party's moderates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quitting' takes C out of CEASES. 'moderates' looks like a noun; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to lessen or soften it, which is what moderating does.

clue.text: Be 4, part of 10?

indicators.note: part of says the letters sit within the answer to clue 10

parts.note: refers to the answer at 10 across, a word meaning attacker

explanation.surface: A cross-reference teaser pointing at two other answers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is SEABORNE, so 'Be 4' means be carried at sea; the answer also sits inside ASSAILANT, the answer to 10.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seaborne is to travel by ship across the water, which is what voyaging by boat means.

clue.text: Wonderful description of Grace?

definitions.meaning: the hymn ... Grace gives Grace this adjective

explanation.definitionFit: Astonishing is a synonym, and the famous hymn title supplies the epithet for Grace.

clue.text: Making a suit?

parts.note: a suit here is a lawsuit, not tailoring; bringing a case to court

explanation.surface: Seems to be about tailoring clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is also a legal action, and pursuing one through the courts is going to law.

clue.text: Wrong one of two writers succeeded

parts.note: Kingsley and Martin Amis, father and son, were both novelists
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: One of a pair of authors was mistaken and still came out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone awry or faulty is described as wrong or out of order.

clue.text: Attacker regularly causes trouble with worker

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of causes

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An assailant reliably makes trouble alongside a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of causes, giving ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assails or physically attacks another is their assailant.

clue.text: Iranian plot is strangely stirring

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so these letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: An Iranian conspiracy is oddly exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges IRANIAN, PLOT and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirring speech rouses and uplifts its listeners, giving them inspiration.

clue.text: Crucial to keep gang looking good

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a pressing matter is urgent, crucial
a posse is a gang or band

explanation.surface: It is vital to keep the crew that looks smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking good' means attractive, not 'appearing well'; the gang slots in after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepossessing appearance is attractive and makes a favourable impression.

clue.text: Rows involved trendier person in church?

indicators.note: involved means twisted and complicated, so these letters are tangled

parts.note: hipper means more fashionable, trendier

explanation.surface: Arguments embroiled a more fashionable churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ROWS into WORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending a church service is there to worship; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Cross-country finished with win

parts.note: over means finished, as in the game is over
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A cross-country race ended in victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling overland means going across the countryside by ground, not sea or air.

clue.text: Unusually gifted person always on the move

indicators.note: unusually means in an unaccustomed way, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkably talented individual who never sits still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges GIFTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person who cannot keep still is called a fidget.

clue.text: Soprano has articles about Les Mis's opening in rep

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the next part

parts.note: A and AN are the indefinite articles

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word Mis's

explanation.surface: A soprano holds forth in some articles about the musical Les Misérables in repertory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' looks like repertory theatre, set up by Les Mis; it is short for representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales rep, or representative, travels selling goods on commission.

clue.text: Not very well-built hotel, blue on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says one word wraps round the other

parts.note: sky blue; the sky is often called the blue
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A flimsy hotel painted blue outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is the sky, as in 'out of the blue', not a colour or a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, scrawny person lacks bulk, so they are hardly well-built.

clue.text: The compiler's favourite American drive

parts.note: the compiler refers to themself as I; compiler's here is compiler is, giving I'M
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: The setter declares a pet American motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the drive or momentum that moves something forward.

clue.text: American overrules first love in calling for time off

indicators.note: overrules means one thing takes the place of another, a swap

parts.note: a vocation is a calling, especially a religious one
love is O, the zero score in tennis; first means the earlier of the two in the word

explanation.surface: An American overrides his first romance in choosing a career and takes a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overrules' puts A in place of the first O in VOCATION. Vacation is the American word for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday from work or study is time off, called a vacation in the US.

clue.text: Trendy drink, we hear, for one in the know

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: we hear means spoken aloud, so the sound gives the letters

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: A fashionable drink, people say, for the well-informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns CIDER into its sound-alike SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation who has privileged information is in the know.

clue.text: I unhappily permit poser to accept one's mistakes

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so a letter is placed inside
unhappily means in an unfortunate state, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; one's is one is, so the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone sadly lets a poser admit their errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second I, from 'one's', is placed among the rearranged letters; 'one's' reads as one is.
explanation.definitionFit: Improprieties are improper acts, lapses of manners or judgment, so breaches or errors.

clue.text: Wet and bright? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: brainy means clever, bright

explanation.surface: A weather report: wet and sunny, but not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright' looks like sunshine; it means clever. 'Not at first' drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with plenty of rainfall is wet.

clue.text: Give up returning some decorative boxes

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters read right to left
boxes means contains, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders the return of a few ornamental boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' holds EDEC across 'some decorative'; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender something, such as territory, is to give it up.

clue.text: Assumption, not new, upset an element

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A supposition, no longer fresh, is overturned by some element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes N from ASSUMPTION; 'upset' rearranges the remaining ASSUMPTIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium is a chemical element, a soft alkali metal with symbol K.

clue.text: Jog naked around front of garden

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: Someone runs unclothed round the front of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like running; it means a gentle push. 'around' puts NUDE round G.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a light push or prod.

clue.text: Food found in two rivers (one short, one Welsh)

parts.note: one river written short is R, its abbreviation
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Something edible turns up where two rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two rivers' frames the pieces: R is river abbreviated and the Usk runs through south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a hard dry biscuit, often given to teething babies.

clue.text: Emptied brandy with lager when drunk, as a rule

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters of brandy

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

indicators.note: drunk suggests something staggering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drains brandy and drinks lager, as is their habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' leaves B and Y of brandy; 'when drunk' rearranges LAGER into LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means generally or on the whole, the same as usually or ordinarily.
